transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um… I guess what brought me in is something my wife’s noticed—well, I’ve noticed it too. She’ll be telling me about things, like my cousin’s appointments or who needs a ride, and I’m looking right at her, like I’m paying attention, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t really take in half of what she said. It’s not that I don’t care, you know? It’s just… I miss it somehow. Does that make sense?
Have you had this kind of trouble taking in what people say since you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wasn’t a bad student or anything—at least I don’t think so—but even back in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but that I was always kind of daydreaming.

They’d say I’d leave homework in my desk, or I’d need reminders to finish classwork. I guess at the time it was just treated like I needed to try a little harder, you know? Does that count as the same kind of thing?
Does this problem with missing what people say also cause trouble for you at work?

Well, I’m not really working a regular job right now, so it’s not like an office situation or anything. But I do help with catering tasks here and there, and I’ve noticed I sometimes have to double-check myself or redo little things so orders or small jobs don’t get mixed up.

It’s not terrible, I don’t think… but it has caused some tension at home too, especially with my cousin’s care. My wife feels like she can’t always count on me to catch the details, and I feel bad about that. Does that answer what you mean?
Has your trouble paying attention gotten noticeably worse in the past year or so?

Yeah… I think it has been a little more noticeable this past year. Not suddenly terrible or anything, but probably for about 11 months now, since my cousin moved in with us after surgery. There’s just been more to keep track of, and I guess it’s made the attention stuff harder to hide or work around. Is that the kind of time frame you mean?
Do you notice this same kind of attention problem in other parts of your life besides home?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, home is where it shows up the most, especially with my cousin’s care—my wife gets frustrated because she feels like she can’t always count on me to catch the details.

But outside of that, with the catering things I help with, I do find myself needing to double-check or fix little things so orders or small jobs don’t get mixed up. It’s not like everything falls apart, but… it does seem to show up there too. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Not really, no. I mean, I can get up and move around like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I feel driven by restlessness or like I can’t sit still. That hasn’t been the main issue for me, I don’t think. Is that what you mean?
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I don’t think so… not in a big way. I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying for no clear reason all the time. At least, it doesn’t feel like that’s the main problem. Is that helpful?
Compared with how you were doing a few years ago, does your attention feel clearly worse now?

Yeah… I’d say it’s been more noticeable lately. Not dramatically worse, I don’t think, but clearly harder than it used to be.

It’s been about, maybe, 11 months or so—since my cousin moved in with us after surgery. That’s when I started noticing I was having a tougher time keeping track of things. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you find yourself forgetting things you were told or events that happened, even later when someone reminds you?

Yeah, a little bit. I wouldn’t say I’m forgetting whole events or anything major, but lately I do forget things I was supposed to do… like returning a call from the doctor’s office, or picking up a prescription.

And sometimes it’s something like leaving the house on time for one of my cousin’s appointments. Someone will remind me and I’ll think, “Oh right, I meant to do that.” It’s embarrassing, but it’s been happening more than I’d like. Does that make sense?
Have you been getting lost in places that should be familiar to you?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I might take a second to remember where I parked or something like that, but I’m not getting lost in familiar places. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you had trouble finding the right words when you’re speaking?

Not really, no. I mean, everybody blanks on a word now and then, and I might do that occasionally, but I haven’t noticed it being a real problem or happening in a way that worries me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When your cousin moved in and you had more responsibilities, did your attention problems become more noticeable because there was simply more to keep track of?

Yes, I think that’s fair. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it did become more noticeable after my cousin moved in with us after surgery. That was about… 11 months ago now.

There was just more to keep track of, and I guess that’s when I started noticing I was having a harder time keeping up. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you ever had a serious head injury?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve bumped my head here and there like anyone, but nothing I’d call serious or that needed major attention. At least nothing comes to mind.
Before age 12, did your attention problems ever cause clear trouble at school, like poor grades or repeated comments from teachers?

Yes… I mean, I did okay in some ways, so I don’t want to overstate it. But before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but that I was always kind of daydreaming. I’d leave homework in my desk sometimes, and I needed reminders to finish classwork.

So, yes, there were comments like that. I’m not sure if you’d call it “clear trouble,” but it was definitely noticed.
Have you ever been told by a doctor that you had a stroke or another brain condition?
No, not that I’m aware of. I’ve never had a doctor tell me I had a stroke or some other brain condition. If something like that had come up, I think I’d remember it.
When you’re not dealing with your cousin’s care, do you still have the same trouble paying attention?

Yes, I think so… maybe not all the time, but it does happen even when it’s not about my cousin.

Like, if I sit down to work out a catering order, or I’m trying to listen through a parish planning call, I start off okay. I really do try to pay attention. But after a while my mind just kind of drifts, and then I’m looking back at the same notes again like I didn’t really read them the first time. It’s not terrible, but yes, it’s there.
Besides at home, has your attention problem caused significant trouble in another setting, such as school, work, or social situations?

Yes… I think outside the home it shows up some, mostly with catering things. I’m not working full-time or anything, but when I help with small catering orders, I’ve had to double-check myself or even redo parts so things don’t get mixed up.

At home it’s probably more obvious, because my wife gets frustrated and feels like she can’t always count on me with my cousin’s care. I don’t mean to make that sound worse than it is, but there has been some tension from it.
Has anyone close to you noticed a clear decline in your memory or thinking compared with how you used to be?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, my wife will point out when I’m not keeping up with something, but I wouldn’t say anyone has said there’s been a clear decline in my memory or thinking compared to before. At least not in those words. If that makes sense.
